title: SPECIMEN 001
name: Bottarga

description.short: Salt-cured grey mullet roe, traditionally produced in Sardinia.
description.long: Prepared for centuries along Mediterranean coasts, bottarga is made from the roe of the grey mullet (Mugil cephalus). Carefully salted, pressed and naturally dried, it has become one of Sardinia's most distinctive culinary traditions, particularly around the Cabras Lagoon.

museumNotes.title: Museum Notes
museumNotes.text: Although today it is considered a delicacy, bottarga originated as a practical method of preserving fish roe. The traditional production process has remained remarkably consistent over generations, relying on salt, pressure, fresh air and time rather than modern industrial techniques.

fieldObservation.title: Field Observation
fieldObservation.text: The Cabras Lagoon, on the western coast of Sardinia, provides one of the most renowned environments for grey mullet fishing. Local knowledge, seasonal rhythms and artisanal methods continue to shape the production of bottarga today.

facts: Prepared from the roe of grey mullet (Mugil cephalus).
Naturally cured using sea salt, pressure and air.
One of the most iconic traditional foods of Sardinia.
